Pathway

QA leadership

For editorial QA lead and content operations roles. These samples show how I would set up a QA process, keep contractors calibrated, and report risk early.

Open these first

  1. WS8 · Editorial operations simulation. Start with the reviewer calibration guide, then the status updates. The scenario is simulated and labeled.
  2. WS7 · Editorial QA case study. The hands-on review behind the process, including the issue log the calibration examples come from.
  3. WS9 · Adult course design. Working with subject matter experts: the review log and how each comment became a decision.
WS8 Simulated scenario

Running a Curriculum Release: An Editorial Operations Simulation

How I would run QA for a team of contract editors.

A simulated curriculum release run end to end: an editorial brief, a QA workflow with checkpoints, a tracker, a reviewer calibration guide, vendor query templates, a change request, a decision log, status updates and a quality scorecard. Team members, timelines and data are simulated and labeled, so it shows method, not track record.

QA process design · Contractor coordination · Quality metricsOpen WS8 →WS7 Reviews real AI output

Editing an AI-Drafted Lesson: An Editorial QA Case Study

A real AI draft, every issue logged, and the clean final side by side.

An AI model was given a lesson brief, and its unedited draft was reviewed as a curriculum editor would: accuracy, alignment, accessibility, style consistency, bias and sources. The case study shows the redline, the issue log by category and severity, the revision cycle, the clean final and a print proofing pass. Every issue is one the draft really had.

Editorial QA · Copyediting · Accessibility review · Print proofingOpen WS7 →WS9 Representative sample

Mentoring New Teachers Through Feedback Conversations

An online and blended course for the people who help new teachers stay.

A short online course with a live session for school leaders and mentors who support teachers in their first three years. Learners study a worked feedback conversation, practice in a branching scenario, check their understanding and plan a real conversation. Includes the design document, LMS structure, storyboard, facilitator guide, usability plan and evaluation plan.

Adult learning · ADDIE · Scenario design · LMS · EvaluationOpen WS9 →

A note on experience

My leadership experience is in academic leadership: as a chief academic officer and dean, I ran curriculum and academic audit processes across campuses and managed staff. I have not managed a team of contract editors; WS8 shows how I would.
